title: The WIMP miracle under siege: direct detection null results
bottleneck: Weakly interacting massive particles were favored because weak-scale thermal relics naturally give the observed dark matter density, but LZ, XENONnT, and PandaX have excluded spin-independent cross sections down to 10^-48 square centimeters with no signal. The surviving WIMP parameter space is increasingly contrived.
why_it_blocks: The WIMP was the most predictive and testable dark matter candidate; its progressive exclusion without a replacement paradigm leaves dark matter phenomenology drifting.
current_state: LZ's latest analyses find no WIMP signal across an ever-widening mass range with world-leading sensitivity, and the field is pivoting toward axions, sterile neutrinos, and ultralight candidates. The neutrino fog, where solar and atmospheric neutrinos mimic dark matter signals, now sets a practical floor for the next generation of detectors.
